newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes eclipsed by Latam activity.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes eclipsed by Latam activity.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes, shut out by the uneconomic trans-Atlantic arbitrage, were eclipsed Monday by spot trading activity in Latin America.
The spread between January West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent continued to widen, reaching $1.10-15 a barrel.
"We're much closer than we have been, but typically the window opens at $1.25-50," one trader said.
Last week, traders speculated that Koch Oil Koch might bring over one of four cargoes of Forties, but the U.S. refiner ended up selling all four into Europe.

Latin trading activity dominated the scene. Venezuelan state owned oil giant Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) bought 380,000 barrels of Ecuadoran Oriente crude from a U.S. refiner for the first week of December.
The price was undisclosed, but traders said Oriente pricing has been aggressive lately, running around West Texas Intermediate minus $2.80-3.00 a barrel.
A PdVSA official asserted that the crude is part of a regular effort to supplement the company's refining system.
"This is not a requirement, we're talking about economic opportunity," the official said.
PdVSA has been buying about a cargo a month of Oriente.
Elsewhere, Argentine YPF is selling 380,000 barrels of Medanito for December 29-30, asking for January WTI minus $1.15 a barrel fob, traders said.
Meanwhile, Bolivia's state owned oil company Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB) is selling 300,000 barrels of reconstituted crude for December 25-30.
Uruguay's state oil refiner ANCAP bought a cargo each of Oriente and Santa Cruz crude for December 7-15.
ANCAP bought the Oriente cargo for Jan WTI minus $2.01 a barrel on a cost-and-freight basis.
The Santa Cruz cargo was sold at Jan WTI minus 45 cents on the same basis.
In the U.S. aftermarket, activity was light. A series of partial January Brent cargoes traded at $23.73 a barrel, 10 cents more than the IPE settlement.
Brent Jan/Feb was done at 62 cents, two cents stronger than the London close.
